text.tspan: What might the sets J and K look like? We expect them to be sets so we'll be defining these "functions" via a
set of ordered pairs. This strips information about the domain and codomain of the function, but is necessary
Let's curry the set {0,1} ≅ {false,true} i.e. the set B = {B₀,B₁}; this should be enough to define a pair of adjoint
functors. We aren't going to review all of c ∈ 𝓒 = Set and d ∈ 𝓓 = Set, but let's check than an isomorphism
exists for the example sets C = {C₀,C₁} and A = {A₀,A₁} (again thinking of these two-element sets as boolean
sets). If this exists, it at least makes a natural isomorpism possible.
We expect an isomorphism J = Set({A₀,A₁},{C₀,C₁}⁽ᴮ⁰ ᴮ¹⁾) ≅ Set({A₀,A₁}×{B₀,B₁},{C₀,C₁}) = K. We can check
these sets have matching sizes |J| = 4² = |K| = 2⁴, so an isomorphism is possible. The set K represents a
boolean function with two inputs and one output, so the 16 binary logical connectives (⊤, ⊥, ↑, etc.). The set J
represents a map from 0/1 to the 4 unary logical connectives (⊤, ⊥, id, ¬). Although we could choose many
possible isomorphisms between these two sets, the expected one likely starts with these mates:
